Subject: EdgeHealth - initial sizing & pricing (draft)

Lena — attached are the results of our quick model run on the 48h sample (summary below). Putting the assumptions up front so you can sanity-check.

Assumptions and observations:
- Traffic: 1.9M req/day (average), peak instantaneous concurrency observed ~1,200 r/s during 60s bursts.
- Prompt sizes: median 280 tokens, 95th 1,200 tokens. Avg response length ~150 tokens.
- Token mix: generation-heavy flows for summarization (long context), and a smaller classification path (short).
- Latency target: <250ms p50, <700ms p95 for conversational endpoints.

Performance and recommended pool:
- Baseline GPU choice: A40-class (mixed inference profile) for best balance of memory & throughput for long contexts.
- Estimated steady-state throughput per GPU: ~45-60 r/s at median context (280 tokens) with batching and KV caching; for 95th-context (1,200 tokens) this drops to ~10-15 r/s.
- Recommended pool to hit 99% of observed peaks with 2x headroom: 24 GPUs (A40 equiv). That supports sustained peaks and allows room for growth and maintenance windows.
- Alternative burst model: 16 GPUs reserved + 8 GPU burst pool (on-demand) to reduce commit size while meeting peak requests.

Pricing & commit options (draft):
- 12-month reserved (24 GPUs): list rate $XX,XXX/month; proposed customer price $YY,YYY/month (~18% off list).
- Hybrid (16 reserved + 8 burst): reserved rate for 16 GPUs at 22% discount; burst billed at on-demand rates with monthly cap.
- Pilot: 2-week technical pilot on 4 GPUs with $10k credit applied to first invoice if customer signs 12mo commit within 30 days. Pilot includes up to 5M tokens/day of evaluation traffic and one integration support sprint.

SLA & guarantees:
- Throughput SLO: we guarantee provisioned throughput for reserved GPUs; Redwood will meet p95 latency targets under the model mix used in sizing. Fallback policy: if model variant cannot meet SLO under heavy tail contexts, automatic routing to a compatible lower-latency variant is available.

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether you want the 24 GPU reserved path or hybrid (16+8).
2) Tell us target sign date so we can lock discount and pilot timing.
3) We can produce an itemized per-token estimate and expected monthly token cost band after you confirm the model family and whether you'll enable KV caching for long contexts.

Attaching: redwood_dedicated_terms_v1.pdf with high-level terms and the attachments you sent for reference.

Cheers,
Karthik
--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Karthik — this is helpful and matches our internal sims closely. A few clarifying Qs: 

1) How sensitive is the 24 GPU recommendation to KV cache hit rate? If we get 60% KV-hit on repeated clinical notes, can we drop reserved to 20 GPUs and rely on burst?
2) For the pilot: can we get the pilot to 30 days and include one SLA exception (90% uptime) so our integration team can validate failover routing?
3) Any flexibility on the commit discount if we do 18mo instead of 12mo? We have procurement cycles that favor 18mo for certs.

Also cc'ing our procurement mailbox (platform@edgehealth.com) to loop in commercial.

Thanks,
Lena
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Lena Park <lena@edgehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-10T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: EdgeHealth - initial sizing & pricing (draft)

Lena — quick answers inline and next steps.

1) KV-hit sensitivity: You can expect roughly linear gains in r/s capacity for generation-heavy workloads as KV-hit increases. With a 60% hit-rate our model runs suggest moving from 24 -> 20 reserved GPUs is reasonable, but we'd still recommend keeping a 6-8 GPU burst pool for headroom on heavy tails. We'll include a sensitivity chart in the final workbook.

2) Pilot extension: We can extend to 30 days but ask that the pilot remain limited to 6 GPUs and include a single SLA exception for non-production validation. If you commit to 18mo within 45 days of pilot end, we'll apply a $15k signing credit and an incremental 2% deeper discount on the reserved rate.

3) 18mo flexibility: Yes — moving to an 18mo term lets us go to a deeper discount band (additional 2-5% depending on GPU count). We'll draft both 12mo and 18mo price ladders so procurement can evaluate.

Action items:
- I'll produce a final workbook w/ sensitivity charts (KV-hit, token length distribution, burst scenarios) and two price ladders (12mo, 18mo).
- Karthik/Marissa will schedule a technical walkthrough for your infra team next week.

If that sounds OK, I'll lock in the pilot credit + 18mo incentive and send an updated commercial term sheet.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
